# Analysis plan

This chapter was written before any outcome was examined. Changes after that
point are logged in the decision record with a reason.

## Estimands

| Question | Population | Outcome | Summary measure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary | All randomized patients with an outcome | Any sore throat at rest, thirty minutes | Odds ratio, licorice vs sugar |
| Secondary | Same | Any sore throat across the four assessments | Population-averaged odds ratio, common and at each assessment |

## Models

1. **First look (sanity check).** Proportions by arm and an unadjusted
   logistic regression at thirty minutes. Randomization makes this the
   primary analysis as well (D-002).
2. **Repeated measures, population-averaged.** Logistic GEE with an
   exchangeable working correlation and robust standard errors. A common
   odds ratio across assessments, and a treatment-by-time model for the odds
   ratio at each assessment (D-003).
3. **Repeated measures, patient-level.** Logistic mixed model with a random
   intercept per patient, fitted by adaptive quadrature. Reported beside the
   GEE because its odds ratio answers a different question (D-004).
4. **Sensitivity.** The primary model adjusted for sex, age, BMI, smoking,
   ASA status and surgery size. Interpreted as a conditional odds ratio, not
   a check of the unadjusted one.
5. **Missing outcomes.** Complete case, with best- and worst-case bounds
   (D-006).

## Verification before trusting a model

Each model function must recover a known effect from simulated data with
the same structure before it is run on the trial data
(`tests/testthat/test-models.R`).

## Reporting

Odds ratios with 95% CI from Wald intervals; p-values to three decimals.
Secondary results are descriptive; no multiplicity adjustment is planned
because there is a single primary comparison.
